text:
tara: Heads-up — we hit a weird edge during the canary for route /v2/generate: quota throttle dropped sampling rate and a small fraction of inspect-mode requests ended up logged unredacted.
kevin: oof. timeline? did the deploy bot show anything?
ops-bot: deploy canary-2026-03-19-4 at 15:08 UTC — rollout 10% -> autoscaled down at 15:22 due to quota breach.
anika: Looks like the quota fallback path sets sampler=100% for debug routes for 2m in code. That interacts badly with the new quota backoff.
samir: Wait — why would debug routes be full-sample on fallback? I thought fallback was to full-redact, not full-sample.
kevin: Historically we favored visibility for oncall and a short-lived breakglass. But that assumed inspect-mode requests are already opt-in consented. Canary revealed some routes called inspect-mode in production via an internal SDK bug.
tara: Right. We had a client bug that toggles inspect on transiently. So breakglass = full-sample caused PII exposure in logs.
morgan: Console UX question: should we expose a per-route "breakglass behavior" toggle (sample|redact|drop) or keep global policy?
anika: Per-route would be safest. Quick proposal:
- If route has "sensitive" tag -> fallback behavior = force-redact
- For non-sensitive debug routes -> allow breakglass-sample with TTL and audit record
- UI shows an explicit review step when enabling breakglass on any route
kevin: +1 for TTL and audit. Also add quota-aware dampening: when quota backoff triggers, prefer degrade to redact rather than increase sample.
samir: Could we patch server to prefer these semantics quickly? Pseudo-config:

```
route: "/v2/generate"
labels: ["debug", "customer-facing"]
sensitive: true
fallback_on_quota: "redact"
breakglass: {enabled: false, ttl_seconds: 0}
```

kevin: That aligns. Implementation tasks:
- (anika) API: add sensitive boolean and fallback enum
- (samir) Runtime: prefer redact path during quota backoff
- (morgan) Console: per-route toggle + explicit confirmation + audit log
- (tara) Ops: rollout canary with a food-safety test (trigger inspect toggle bug) and validate no unredacted logs
anika: One edge: telemetry. If we always redact on quota, metrics for sample counts drop and can hide some regressions. We should emit a telemetry-only counter (no payload) showing how many requests were forced-redact.
kevin: Yes — telemetry counter name: request_forced_redact{route,reason=quota|policy}
samir: Make sure that counter doesn't include request body or any identifiers. Just tags/labels.
morgan: UX: console should show a small yellow badge on routes with forced-redact events in last 24h and link to the aggregate metric (not logs).
tara: Tests: add automated end-to-end that simulates quota backoff and asserts no plain text request/response logged. Also add mutation test for transient inspect flag.
anika: I'll open a PR with schema changes + migration plan. Quick mitigation patch: default fallback for all routes -> redact unless explicitly opt-in via a 'breakglass-allow' flag scoped to team and audited.
kevin: Rollout plan: patch in staging, run canary at 5% for 24h, run the simulated client-bug flood for 30m. If green, promote and then flip console toggle for teams that request breakglass.
samir: Ops runbook update: add checklist to check request_forced_redact counter and account for quota-related spikes.
ops-bot: incident-note created: IN-2026-03-19-01 "canary-unredacted-logs" assigned to tara, severity: low->med (investigating)
kevin: Thx. One follow-up — we should audit historical logs for the 14m window. Tara, can you kick that off with an automated scan that only flags entries where inspect=true and redaction_missing=true? Keep results in encrypted storage.
tara: On it. I'll paste the scan query once I have it. For now I'm toggling the global fallback to redact in prod immediately (small safety change).
morgan: I'll draft the console confirmation modal copy: "Enabling breakglass sampling may expose sensitive data. Confirm you have authorization and an audit plan." Include checkbox for "I understand".
anika: Cool. I'll include the telemetry counters and config bits in my PR description. 
kevin: Great coordination. Let's keep replies here — if anyone wants to diverge, open a thread.
samir: Quick note: add e2e to CI that asserts telemetry-only counters are emitted even when payloads are redacted, this will prevent silent telemetry regressions.
tara: Agreed. I pushed the immediate fallback toggle. Will report back after the historic scan.
kevin: :thumbsup:
